question: What is the smallest version 1.3 guest-owned Xbox System Link discovery boundary after the general XGI session-search hypothesis is rejected?

scope.boundary: This checkpoint identifies the exact QoS lookup and release wrappers, the sole lookup producer, the first result-word progress gate, the release caller, the exact fixed-size request-buffer producer that feeds downstream indexed callbacks, the game-selector AVM1 producer for FSCommand:OnPressY, the native 10-byte FSCommand prefix gate and two neutral callback sites, one controlled runtime receiver and target tuple at callback site 0x8220B4C0, the target's exact vtable slot and neutral two-stage virtual-forwarding shape, a bounded zero-match split-constant search for the observed vtable base, a bounded OnPressY/OnPressX command-reference chain, a bounded negative for direct uses of the exact GFX_GameSelector.gfx guest string, and a bounded zero-match runtime probe at exact function entry 0x82DECB20. It does not identify the observed receiver's class or visible action owner, either downstream virtual method's semantics, or message or buffer-record semantics, advertisement or discovery behavior, host/client direction, delivery, matchmaking, transport, relay, or Internet play.

currentEvidence.method: Five owner-bounded groups of eight foreground read-only Ghidra packets against the pinned image, followed by one dispatcher setup-only packet, three resource-name packets, seven FSCommand-boundary packets, and two separately bounded default-off runtime probes, with narrow generated-code corroboration only after exact function identification
currentEvidence.qualification: The visible System Link label owner is UI-only and the visible Refresh and Create Game strings have no modeled references. Exact game-selector AVM1 maps Key.getCode() value 45 to FSCommand:OnPressY, and exact guest code recognizes the FSCommand: prefix before two neutral callback sites. One controlled runtime trace observed that exact command at 0x8220B4C0 with receiver 0x509201FC, readable leading word 0x82162F34, and dynamic target 0x82C7CBE0. Static follow-up places that target at vtable slot +0x04 and closes a two-stage virtual-forwarding shape. The vtable base has zero modeled direct references and zero bounded same-block split-constant constructions, but those negatives do not exclude an indirect producer or runtime store. No object class, downstream method semantic, visible game-list owner, or networking behavior is identified. Matching OnPressY and OnPressX resource and guest-image strings provide search guidance into exact function 0x82DECB20, but its bounded command chain does not implement or dispatch either command. Exact guest string GFX_GameSelector.gfx has no modeled reference, bounded split-address code use, or aligned initialized-memory pointer placement. A corrected default-off runtime probe at exact function entry 0x82DECB20 produced no matching line during one controlled System Link game-list Y press and captured no receiver identity. Exact message 0x000B001B is submitted with the fixed-size buffer later consumed as the input record collection for the QoS lookup path, but one controlled default-off runtime probe produced no matching request and Xbox static evidence does not prove that the message populates the buffer or name either one.

uiAnchors.qualification: The visible Refresh and Create Game label strings have zero modeled references. Exact game-selector AVM1 supplies an OnPressY producer and the guest image supplies an FSCommand prefix gate and neutral callback boundary. One controlled trace observed exact OnPressY at callback site 0x8220B4C0 with receiver 0x509201FC, readable leading word 0x82162F34, and dynamic target 0x82C7CBE0. Static follow-up places the target at vtable slot +0x04 and shows it forwards through two further virtual calls. The vtable base has zero modeled direct references and zero bounded same-block split-constant constructions, but no object class, downstream method semantic, or visible menu owner is proved. Exact OnPressY and OnPressX each have one defined guest-image string and one modeled parameter reference in exact function 0x82DECB20. That function does not implement either action. Its exact callees recognize only OnLoadUnitStack, OnClearUnitStack, OnAccept, OnCancel, OnOption, OnInit, OnExit, PlaySound, and StopSound. Exact 0x82DECB20 has one modeled data-pointer placement at 0x82128750 and no modeled direct caller. The seven-word pointer neighborhood is recorded without table, slot, class-boundary, or ownership claims. Exact guest string GFX_GameSelector.gfx at 0x8211FFB0 has zero modeled references, zero bounded same-block split-address uses, and zero aligned initialized-memory pointer placements. This exhausts the direct static resource-name anchor without proving that the runtime resource system never derives or consumes the name. The corrected exact-entry runtime probe produced zero matches for one controlled Y press and captured no receiver identity. No networking behavior is established.

qosLookup.forwarding: The wrapper inserts literal caller value 1 as import arg1, shifts incoming register args r3 through r10 to import args2 through 9, copies four incoming stack arguments to import args10 through 13, and returns the import result unchanged.
qosLookup.producerArguments: The producer passes the copied record count, the three parallel array bases, three zero values, literal 8, three further zero values, and the address of object slot +0x98C.
qosLookup.resultSlot: Before lookup, object slot +0x98C is initialized to object address +0x96C. The cleanup path later passes the slot value to NetDll_XNetQosRelease when non-null; whether lookup replaces the pointer and how release treats it remain unresolved.
qosLookup.returnUse: The producer returns true exactly when the lookup wrapper returns zero.
qosLookup.qualification: The thirteen-argument import shape, producer arrays, output slot, success test, first result-word progress gate, and release path are exact. Public argument names and the per-entry result layout remain unresolved in Xbox guest evidence.

qosResultLifecycle.progressGate: A null result bypasses this gate. For a non-null result, a zero word permits the enclosing state field to advance from literal 2 to literal 3; a nonzero word retains state 2.
qosResultLifecycle.releasePointer: The release caller reads object slot +0x98C and tail-calls the wrapper only when the pointer is non-null. Static evidence does not establish whether lookup replaced the initial embedded pointer.
qosResultLifecycle.qualification: Result offset +0x04 is a neutral progress-gate word in Xbox guest evidence. External layout names, allocation mechanics, asynchronous signaling, and the meanings of enclosing states 2 and 3 are not promoted.

downstreamCollection.vtableProof: Exact teardown helper 0x82C9CCF8 installs leading pointer 0x82160450.
downstreamCollection.collectionField: enclosing object +0x24, a non-null 1334-byte request buffer on the producer's successful allocation path
downstreamCollection.countRead: The state function reads the buffer pointer and then its leading word as the iteration count.
downstreamCollection.lookupInputLink: Before calling producer 0x82C99628, the state function copies enclosing-object field +0x24 into lookup-object field +0x04 and zeroes lookup-object result slot +0x98C. The producer reads the same collection's leading count through field +0x04.
downstreamCollection.downstreamUse: After the result-word progress gate, the state function enters downstream virtual callbacks only when its downstream object field is non-null. On its byte-flag-zero branch it invokes one callback per collection index and then one final callback. It reads no completed QoS per-entry field before any downstream call.
downstreamCollection.zeroCountPath: When the linked collection count is zero, producer 0x82C99628 returns before calling NetDll_XNetQosLookup, leaving the pre-zeroed result slot null. The state function then takes its null-result bypass and can continue into the separately guarded downstream path.
downstreamCollection.qualification: This separates the indexed request buffer from the QoS result in the exact local path. It does not identify callback semantics, buffer-record meaning, visible Refresh ownership, advertisement source, or discovery mechanism.

requestBufferProducer.sizeProbe: With a size below 1334 or a null buffer, 0x82A1F3F0 writes required size 1334 and returns 122 without issuing its message.
requestBufferProducer.bufferField: The producer allocates the required byte count and stores the returned pointer at enclosing-object field +0x24.
requestBufferProducer.submission: The second helper call supplies the allocated buffer and enclosing-object field +0x28 as a completion pointer. The producer accepts return zero or 997 and then sets field +0x1C to one.
requestBufferProducer.requestRecord: The 20-byte record contains the function's 32-bit second argument at +0x00, a neutral 64-bit word at +0x04, the buffer size at +0x0C, and the buffer pointer at +0x10.
requestBufferProducer.qualification: Both exact message edges require narrow generated-code corroboration after Ghidra truncation. Xbox static evidence supplies no semantic message name, result record layout, visible Refresh ownership, completion behavior, discovery source, or runtime delivery.

Do not interpret the retained 72-byte QoS listener payload without a separately closed guest consumer layout.
Do not assign semantic names to messages 0x000B001B or 0x00058023 from this static evidence.
Do not implement the 1334-byte buffer record layout; the controlled action did not reach the exact request and produced no write-extent or completion evidence.
Do not implement per-entry result records from external source alone.
Do not expect NetDll_XNetQosLookup alone to create a missing downstream collection entry in the exact zero-count path.
Do not assign a receiver class or visible action owner from the single observed FSCommand receiver, leading word, and dynamic target tuple.
Do not assign semantics to the observed FSCommand target's two downstream virtual calls from their slot offsets or forwarding shape.
Do not treat zero modeled direct references or split-constant constructions of vtable base 0x82162F34 as proof that no constructor, indirect producer, or runtime store exists.
Do not claim discovery, matchmaking, delivery, host authority, transport, relay, Internet play, or Game of the Week behavior from this evidence.
conclusion: Exact request producer 0x82C9CF70 remains a supported version 1.3 System Link lead: it runs prerequisite message 0x00058023, probes for a fixed 1334-byte buffer, stores a non-null allocation at field +0x24, and submits message 0x000B001B with a 20-byte request record and a completion pointer. Exact state function 0x82C9D338 later uses that buffer's leading count to feed QoS lookup producer 0x82C99628, then gates progress on neutral QoS result word +0x04. One controlled default-off runtime probe did not reach the exact request. Exact game-selector AVM1 proves that Key.getCode() value 45 produces FSCommand:OnPressY. Exact guest code recognizes the 10-byte FSCommand: prefix through comparator 0x827F43F0, strips it, and reaches receiver-vtable slot +0x04 callback sites 0x8220A634 and 0x8220B4C0. One controlled default-off trace observed the first exact OnPressY once at 0x8220B4C0 with receiver 0x509201FC, readable leading word 0x82162F34, and dynamic target 0x82C7CBE0. Static follow-up confirms that target at vtable slot +0x04 and closes a neutral two-stage virtual-forwarding shape through the callback's second argument. The vtable base has zero modeled direct references and zero bounded same-block split-constant constructions, which does not exclude an indirect producer or runtime store. This does not identify either object class, either downstream method's semantics, or the visible action owner. The separate command-reference function 0x82DECB20 and its three bounded callees handle only generic UI and unit-stack commands, and its corrected runtime probe produced zero matching lines during one controlled Y press. Do not retry 0x82DECB20 or resume adjacent reads. Stop at an owner checkpoint. If the owner separately continues this exact evidence chain, the smallest candidate is one bounded initialized-memory pointer search for exact value 0x82162F34, capped at eight placements without following any result. Message, record, visible action, advertisement, discovery, and ordering semantics remain unresolved.
